findings.evidence: `pkg/ddl/backfilling_dist_scheduler.go` `generatePlanForPhysicalTable`: (1) `startKey, endKey, err := getTableRange(...); if startKey == nil && endKey == nil { return nil, nil }` runs before `if err != nil`, so `(nil,nil,err)` is treated as empty and the error is dropped. (2) Inside `handle.RunWithRetry(...)`, TS allocation failures do `importTS, err := allocNewTS(...); if err != nil { return true, nil }`. `handle.RunWithRetry` returns immediately on `err == nil` (`pkg/disttask/framework/handle/handle.go` in this commit), so this does not retry and can return a partially-filled `subTaskMetas` slice as a “successful” plan.
findings.fix: In `generatePlanForPhysicalTable`: (a) check `err` from `getTableRange` before the `(nil,nil)` empty-table fast-path; (b) on `allocNewTS` failure return `(true, err)` (or `(true, errors.Trace(err))`) so `RunWithRetry` actually retries; (c) build metas in a local slice inside the retry closure and only assign/append to the outer slice when the closure completes successfully to avoid partial plans leaking; (d) for `shouldRetry`, return a retryable non-nil error (sentinel) instead of `(true, nil)`.
findings.impact: Silent plan truncation or empty-plan generation can skip some (or all) record key ranges, causing add-index backfill to miss rows and leave the new index incomplete (wrong query results; potential uniqueness/consistency issues). This PR newly routes partition tables through this plan generator, expanding the blast radius from non-partition tables to partitioned tables as well.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Not fixed on `upstream/master`: `pkg/ddl/backfilling_dist_scheduler.go` still returns `(true, nil)` on `allocNewTS` failure and still checks `(startKey==nil && endKey==nil)` before `err`; `pkg/dxf/framework/handle/handle.go` still stops retrying when `err == nil` regardless of the retryable bool.
findings.verify: Add a unit/integration test (or failpoint) that forces `allocNewTS` to fail after N successful allocations during plan generation; assert `OnNextSubtasksBatch` returns a non-nil error and does not return a partial `metas` slice. Add a test forcing `getTableRange` to return `(nil,nil,err)` (e.g., injected iterateSnapshotKeys error) and assert the error propagates instead of producing an empty plan.
findings.what: `generatePlanForPhysicalTable` can silently return partial/empty subtask plans by swallowing planning-time errors (notably `allocNewTS` failures and potentially `getTableRange` errors). With this PR, partitioned tables now use this function, so an intermittent PD/GetTS or snapshot-range error can lead to an incomplete add-index backfill without the framework noticing.

subject: ddl: split partition tables subtasks like normal tables (#59407)
summary: Partition tables now use the same region-splitting plan generator as normal tables, but the planner can silently drop errors and return partial/empty subtask lists, risking incomplete add-index backfill; the issue remains present on upstream/master.
